extracted.intended_audience: peer reviewers/referees invited to review for Scientific Reports
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for researchers acting as referees for manuscripts submitted to the journal Scientific Reports, covering what to assess in manuscripts and how to conduct the review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication criteria: scientific validity and technical soundness
rubrics_metrics.description: To be published in Scientific Reports, a paper must be scientifically valid and technically sound in methodology and analysis. Manuscripts are not assessed based on their perceived importance, significance or impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal accepts niche scope, interdisciplinary work, negative results, and scientifically-justified replications. Focus review on whether the methods and analysis are appropriate and properly conducted, and whether conclusions are supported by the data, rather than on perceived importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary purpose of the review
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide Editorial Board Members with the information needed to reach a decision and instruct the authors on how they can strengthen their manuscript to the point where it may be acceptable for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports should give editors clear evidence-based judgements about technical soundness and should offer constructive guidance for authors on how to address problems or strengthen the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical soundness / scientific validity
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the manuscript on technical soundness and scientific validity: methods must be appropriate and properly conducted, and the conclusions drawn must be fully supported by the data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify methodological flaws, inappropriate techniques, insufficient controls, or other problems that undermine validity. Distinguish between fixable issues and fundamental flaws that warrant rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Are the claims convincing?
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether the claims made are convincing; if not, specify what further evidence is needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be specific about missing experiments, analyses, or controls that would make claims convincing. Where possible, suggest feasible additional work or analyses rather than vague criticisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims supported by experimental data
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the authors' claims are fully supported by the experimental data presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out instances of overinterpretation or conclusions that go beyond the data. Indicate which claims are supported and which require more evidence or rephrasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical analysis is sound
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether the statistical analysis of the data is appropriate and correctly performed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for correct choice of tests, proper handling of multiple comparisons, reporting of effect sizes/confidence intervals where appropriate, sample size justification, and clear description of statistical methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data availability standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the availability of data adheres to the expected standards of the research community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check compliance with journal policies and community norms for data deposition, code availability, and transparency. Flag missing datasets or inaccessible code that prevent verification of results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextualisation within previous literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the claims are appropriately discussed in the context of the previous literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify missing citations, misrepresentation of prior work, or failure to place results in appropriate conceptual context. Suggest literature the authors should consider citing or discussing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential for resubmission / promise of the study
rubrics_metrics.description: If the manuscript is unacceptable in its present form, determine whether the study seems sufficiently promising that authors should be encouraged to consider a resubmission in the future.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate whether issues are addressable (major revisions) or fundamental (reject). If encouraging resubmission, specify the key changes or additional work required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and accessibility of writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the manuscript is clearly written; if not, provide suggestions to make it more accessible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out unclear sections, poor organization, ambiguous wording, or presentation problems (figures/tables) and suggest concrete improvements to enhance readability and comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical concerns (animals / human subjects)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify any special ethical concerns arising from the use of animals or human subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag missing ethical approvals, inadequate consent procedures, noncompliance with guidelines, or other ethical issues that could preclude publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neutrality on jurisdictional claims and naming conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific Reports remains strictly neutral with respect to jurisdictional claims in published maps and institutional affiliations; naming conventions are left to authors' discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referees should not request changes to such matters unless it is critical to the clarity of the scientific content of the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not assess importance or impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Referees are asked not to assess the importance, significance or impact of a paper; the research community will judge this after publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus the review on validity, technical soundness, and clarity rather than novelty or expected influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Willingness to provide follow-up advice
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should be willing to provide further advice on a revised manuscript if requested by the Editorial Board Member.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors may reconsult original reviewers after resubmission, but will not return a manuscript to reviewers if authors have not made a serious attempt to address criticisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer selection factors (for editors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial Board Members choose referees based on multiple factors including expertise, specific recommendations, and previous experience. Invitations to review are confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This explains why reviewers are selected and underscores confidentiality of the invitation process; useful context for referees about expectations and selection rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI use by peer reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers should not upload manuscripts into generative AI tools, and must transparently declare any use of AI tools in their evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanation: generative AI has limitations and may produce false, biased, or nonsensical information; manuscripts can contain sensitive or proprietary information that should not be shared with third-party AI services. If any part of the evaluation was supported by an AI tool, declare it in the peer review report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial Board Members and reviewers must treat the review process as strictly confidential and should not discuss the manuscript with anyone not directly involved in the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consulting with laboratory colleagues is acceptable but they should be identified to the Editorial Board Member. Consulting outside experts may be acceptable but check with the Editorial Board Member first to avoid involving excluded parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are asked to provide a report promptly; ideally within 10 days of receiving a manuscript, but extensions may be arranged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a delay is anticipated, inform the Editorial Board Member and publishing office so authors can be kept informed and alternative referees found if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymity policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific Reports does not release reviewers' identities to authors or other reviewers unless reviewers specifically ask to be identified; reviewers are preferred to remain anonymous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referees should not identify themselves to authors without the Editorial Board Member's knowledge. If a reviewer wishes to reveal their identity, this should be done via the publishing office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing of referees' reports
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal does not edit reviewer reports; comments intended for the authors are transmitted as written, except in rare cases to remove offensive language or confidential information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referees should avoid comments that cause needless offence, though robustly-expressed criticisms are acceptable. Editors may remove offensive content or confidential details in rare circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competing interests / conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Referees should draw attention to anything that might affect their review and decline invitations if they feel unable to be objective (e.g., recent collaborations, draft comments, direct competition, financial interest).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors recognize conflicts are not always clear-cut and being close to the field does not automatically invalidate a report. Previous review for another journal is not by itself a reason to decline. Declare potential biases so editors can weigh reports appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online manuscript review submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Referees must submit their comments via the journal's online submission system using the link in the invitation email.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For technical help with the manuscript tracking system, contact the journal support team. Do not send review comments outside the official system.
